text.p: (Figures in millions of French francs unless stated)
NOTE - French drinks group Remy-Cointreau said in a statement that first quarter turnover to end June rose 13.4 percent to 1.45 billion francs.
It said first quarter turnover showed growth in all divisions. "This performance reflects the good health of the brands and the dynamism of the commercial network," the company said.
Contribution to oper result by branch
NOTE - Remy-Cointreau said in its earnings statement that it would propose a net dividend per share of 4.60 francs, identical to that of the previous year, at a board meeting on August 26.
It said the improvement in the financial result reflected a drop in the debt in 1995/96. Debt increased in 1996/97 due to the acquisition of the Venoge brand and the group's sales rise.

The drop in operating profit for Remy Martin cognacs was due partly to higher marketing investments and lower sales in Japan and Taiwan, not fully compensated by "satisfying activity" in China and the United States, it said.
The drop in the spirits/liquors division's operating profit was due to important investments in marketing and new products.
The champagne business was boosted by higher sales and higher sales prices, and the wines business was helped by strong demand for Bordeaux wines.
The exceptional result includes 277 million francs in restructuring charges for coming years, partially offset by 176 million francs in gains from asset sales and financial products.
Promotional expenses were increased by 100 million francs.
